episodes.title: Venture into Shakahola Forest
episodes.description: Shakahola Forest presents a harsh and unforgiving landscape characterized by dry coastal woodland and thick bush vegetation. The terrain is largely covered by indigenous shrubs, scattered trees, thorny thickets, and dense undergrowth that make movement through the area both difficult and physically demanding. The forest's vastness and dense vegetation provide limited visibility in many sections, making it difficult to see beyond a short distance. Some areas are relatively open, while others are heavily overgrown, creating a sense of isolation and remoteness.

episodes.title: This is where we lived - Court visits Pastor Paul Nthenge Mackenzie homestead in Shakahola
episodes.description:
At Mackenzie’s homestead, the court was shown several structures that witnesses say served different purposes within the settlement. Among them was a meeting area where elders, including Mackenzie, allegedly sat to resolve disputes. The compound also contained bedrooms, a kitchen, toilet facilities, and a bathroom.

This homestead has featured prominently throughout the proceedings, with numerous witnesses and investigators referring to activities that allegedly took place there.

A witness further told the court that Mackenzie’s residence stood in stark contrast to those of his followers. Unlike the modest structures occupied by many congregants, Mackenzie’s house and toilet facilities were reportedly well-finished, neatly thatched, and equipped with a water pan situated outside the compound.

According to the witness, the structures in Mackenzie homestead were in contrast to those of his followers as his house and toilet facilities were reportedly well finished, neatly thatched, and had a water pan situated outside his compound.

episodes.title: Inside Shakahola
episodes.description:
Accompanied by parties to the case, including representatives from the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions, investigators from the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, and other stakeholders, the court ventured deeper into the forest. There, it observed remnants of structures where followers are said to have lived.

Shakahola Forest presents a harsh and unforgiving landscape characterized by dry coastal woodland and thick bush vegetation. The terrain is largely covered by indigenous shrubs, scattered trees, thorny thickets, and dense undergrowth that make movement through the area both difficult and physically demanding. The forest's vastness and dense vegetation provide limited visibility in many sections, making it difficult to see beyond a short distance. Some areas are relatively open, while others are heavily overgrown, creating a sense of isolation and remoteness.

The team also visited the assembly point under the native "Mitola" tree, a location that witnesses allege served as a gathering place for Mackenzie’s followers before the onset of fasting and resultant death in 2023. The site has been repeatedly mentioned in testimony as a place where followers met for teachings and other activities.

episodes.title: Shakahola case updates 14 10 24 720
episodes.description:
The Shakahola cases in Shanzu, Mombasa, Malindi, and Tononoka Law Courts have drawn significant attention both locally and internationally. At the heart of this issue is the arrest and prosecution of Paul Mackenzie and 93 others, whose actions have been linked to extremism, terrorism, cruelty to a child, and infringing a child's right to education. 

Key witnesses and their testimonies have been critical in unraveling the events that led to the four cases against Mackenzie and others, shedding light on the circumstances surrounding the acts of extremism, terrorism, murder, manslaughter, and crimes against children. episodes.title: Shakahola manslaughter case opening statement
episodes.description: An opening statement in a case where Pastor Paul Nthege Mackenzie and 94 others are charged before the Chief Magistrate Court in Mombasa with 238 counts of manslaughter contrary to Section 202, as read with Section 205 of the penal code.

episodes.description: An update of case where Paul Nthege Mackenzie and 94 others are charged with terrorism related charges related to Shakahola massacre .

episodes.title: DPP's Opening statement on Shakahola children case
episodes.description: Prosecution Opening Statement in a case where Pastor Paul Mackenzie and 38 other  Shakahola massacre suspects, who are parents of children victims rescued from Shakahola forest were are charged before the Tononoka Children Court in Mombasa with children-related offences such as subjecting children to torture, assault, cruelty to children, and infringing a child's right to education.
